files.purpose: Adaptation, deployment, duplicate-policy, security, validation, and rollback guidance
License for the public recipe package

Rerunnable stable-key WorkflowType, attribute, activity, action, and setting deployment

instructions: Review the immutable README, mapping contract, Lava deploy, SQL verifier, and static test before adaptation.
Create the target Connection Request attributes and complete every required value in the deploy's ADAPTATION REQUIRED block.
Run the deploy from a temporary administrator-only Lava Application endpoint with only RockEntity, RockEntityModify, and read-only Sql enabled.
Run the deploy twice and require stable reuse plus zero invalid Create Connection Request references.
Review the workflow in Rock, then assign it manually as the registration template's Registrant Workflow.
Submit a marked test registration through the real registration experience and run the read-only verifier.
Document retry and backfill duplicate behavior before processing any existing registrants.
known_limitations: The sanitized deployment has not been executed unchanged against every supported Rock release or plugin combination.
The native registration trigger is expected to launch once per new registrant; manual reruns and backfills require an explicit duplicate policy.
The example includes one generic mapped value and must be extended carefully for additional fields and field-type normalization.
Connection Request attribute qualifiers vary by local Connection configuration and must be created and permissioned before deployment.
An empty registration campus remains empty; the recipe intentionally does not substitute the person's primary campus.
learnings: Registrant-scoped automation should use the template's Registrant Workflow and consume RegistrationRegistrantId rather than guessing from registrar or person context.
Create Connection Request falls back to the person's primary campus when no Campus Attribute is configured, so registration campus must be wired explicitly when it is authoritative.
Capture the created request in a workflow attribute before later native actions copy request attributes.
Store the source Registration ID and construct local links when rendering instead of persisting environment-specific URLs.
Use stable ForeignKeys and re-query canonical IDs after every modify operation so rerunnable deploys do not depend on transient return objects.
Validate that all action-setting attribute GUIDs belong to the same WorkflowType; stale cross-workflow references can survive copied configuration.
Keep deployment SQL read-only and use native Rock actions for runtime writes.
Treat retries and backfills as a separate reviewed workflow because unconditionally rerunning Create Connection Request can create duplicates.
outcomes: Each newly submitted registrant can launch a workflow that creates a native Connection Request.
The request records the source Registration ID without persisting an environment-specific admin URL.
Registration campus, comments, and explicitly mapped values are available to authorized Connections staff.
prerequisites: A target Connection Type, Opportunity, and Status reviewed for the intended follow-up process.
A registration template with the required registrant attributes and permission to assign a Registrant Workflow.
Pre-created Connection Request attributes for source registration traceability and every mapped value.
A temporary admin-only Lava Application deployment endpoint with RockEntity, RockEntityModify, and read-only Sql commands.
A nonproduction environment and marked test registration for end-to-end validation.
rollback_steps: Remove the workflow from the registration template's Registrant Workflow setting so new submissions stop launching it.
Deactivate the deployed WorkflowType and restore any prior template workflow assignment.
Review marked test Connection Requests manually; do not bulk-delete requests or AttributeValues through this recipe.
Disable or remove the temporary admin deployment endpoint after rollback verification.

security.authentication: Rock-authenticated administrator for deployment; runtime launch follows the registration submission and workflow context configured by Rock.
security.authorization: Deployment is limited to trusted administrators, while Connection Type, page, attribute, workflow, and reporting permissions limit resulting data to approved staff.
notes: The deployment endpoint changes Rock configuration and should be disabled or removed after use.
Runtime writes use native Create Connection Request and Set Entity Attribute actions; SQL in the package is read-only lookup and verification.
Registration answers can contain pastoral, contact, care, or other sensitive information; copy only fields staff need.
Do not persist a full admin URL because it leaks environment routing and becomes stale across hosts.
The reference does not delete or merge existing requests and must not be used as a bulk cleanup tool.

summary: Create a Connection Request for each selected registration registrant, preserve source traceability, copy registration campus explicitly, and transfer reviewed attributes through native Rock workflow actions.
title: Registration-to-Connection Request Transfer Workflow
use_cases: Move application or intake registration data into a Connection Board for staff follow-up.
Create one Connection Request per registrant while preserving a traceable source Registration ID.
Carry the registration's selected campus and reviewed registrant attributes into the follow-up process.
validation_steps: Run python3 tests/static_contract.py from the recipe directory.
Confirm the deploy stops while local opportunity, status, or target attribute configuration is missing.
Run the deploy twice and confirm exactly one managed WorkflowType, one Start activity, nine workflow attributes, and stable managed actions remain.
Confirm every Create Connection Request setting GUID resolves to an attribute qualified to the deployed WorkflowType.
Submit one marked test registrant and confirm exactly one Connection Request has the expected person, opportunity, status, and comments.
Confirm ConnectionRequest.CampusId equals Registration.CampusId, including a deliberate null-campus case.
Confirm the source registration attribute stores RegistrationRegistrant.RegistrationId and the mapped target value matches its source.
Run tests/verify-transfer.sql with a read-only principal and confirm MatchingRequestCount is one and CampusMatches is true.
Manually retry only under the documented duplicate policy and verify no unintended duplicate is created.
